industry: Family Footwear Retail (Shoe Carnival / Shoe Station / Rogan's banners)
drawdown_context: SCVL is a 46-year-old, founder-controlled (Weaver family ~33.8%) family-footwear retailer that closed FY24 (52 weeks ended Feb 1, 2025) with $1.20B Net Sales (+2.3% YoY), $91.2M Operating Income, $73.8M Net Income, $123.1M cash + marketable securities, zero debt for the 20th consecutive year, and a freshly raised quarterly dividend ($0.135 -> $0.150 announced March 12, 2025). The 'distress' label here is mechanical (removed from S&P 600 between 2025-05-15 and 2026-05-15), not financial. The drawdown into mid-May 2025 reflects (i) a guided -$20-25M Operating Income hit from the just-announced 175-store Shoe Station rebanner program disclosed in the March 2025 10-K (~25% of FY24 OI), (ii) -3.9% FY24 comparable stores Net Sales with Shoe Carnival banner -mid-single-digits and a flagged -5% physical traffic decline, (iii) Nike/Skechers/Crocs vendor concentration at 48% of Net Sales (Nike alone 24%, up from 14% in FY22) into a Hispanic-skew customer base exposed to consumer-spending softness and 2025 tariff regime risk. No going concern, no covenant amendment, no auditor change, no insider flight pattern.

summary: SCVL is an honest-disclosure family footwear retailer caught in an operational drawdown, not a distressed company. The 10-K (filed Mar 21, 2025) and Q3 FY24 10-Q (Dec 6, 2024) together confirm: 20 consecutive years with zero funded debt, $123.1M cash + marketable securities, $99M undrawn on a $100M facility with affirmative covenant compliance, no going-concern language, Deloitte (Big-4) as auditor with attested ICFR and no Item 9 disagreements, dividend RAISED 11.1% to $0.150/sh on March 12, 2025 (8 weeks before cutoff), and Rogan's acquisition Year-1 targets exceeded with standalone metrics disclosed. The buyback authorization ($50M, Dec 11 2024) is untouched -- the OPPOSITE of the MGPI trough-buyback-defense pattern. Claim evolution from the December Q3 10-Q to the March 10-K is consistent (no story drift on comps, boots, hurricanes, or warm-weather attribution). The real risks are operational and disclosed transparently: (i) Nike concentration drift from 14% to 24% of Net Sales in two years with no long-term contract, (ii) the 175-store Shoe Station rebanner being scaled 17.5x from a 10-store test with <12-month look-back and no per-store dispersion data, (iii) a $20-25M FY25 OI hit (~25% of FY24 OI) from rebanner cost amortization, (iv) China sourcing tariff exposure flagged but not quantified for pass-through. The only true Mode B yellow flag the framework cannot exonerate under blinding is the Mar 14, 2025 four-filing Form 4 cluster between FY-end and 10-K filing (could be benign vesting, could be opportunistic sells). Verdict: NEUTRAL with a slight LONG-tier honesty-alpha tilt -- SCVL is the type of name the framework EXCLUDES the lying-distress short on, even though the operating outlook is genuinely soft. Composite in the 0.30-0.35 range correctly reflects 3 MODERATE_UNDERDELIVERY (vendor concentration sensitivity gap, rebanner evidence gap, tariff pass-through silence; all operational not deceptive) + 1 UNVERIFIABLE (insider Form 4 cluster) against 6 firm PASSes on the balance-sheet/auditor/dividend/buyback/Rogan's/claim-evolution battery.
